introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is a homologous series?

(ii) To which homologous series does ethanol belong? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A homologous series is a **family of organic compounds with the same functional group and the same general formula**, in which each member differs from the next by a $-\mathrm{CH_2}-$ unit. Members have similar chemical properties and their physical properties change gradually along the series.

(ii) Ethanol belongs to the **alcohols (alkanols)**, general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$, functional group $-\mathrm{OH}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the first member of this homologous series. *[1 mark]*
State the observation when $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ is added to a solution of ethanol. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Steamy (white) fumes** of hydrogen chloride gas are evolved: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{PCl_5} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_5Cl} + \mathrm{POCl_3} + \mathrm{HCl}$. This is the test for the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the reagent and reaction conditions necessary to convert:

(i) Ethanol to ethene. Reagent: ......... Condition: .........

(ii) Ethanol to ethyl ethanoate. Reagent: ......... Condition: ......... *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Ethanol to ethene (dehydration): **Reagent:** concentrated sulphuric acid ($\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$), or alumina ($\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$) as catalyst. **Condition:** heat strongly, about $170^\circ$C (excess acid).
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_4} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

(ii) Ethanol to ethyl ethanoate (esterification): **Reagent:** ethanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$) with a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid as catalyst. **Condition:** warm (heat gently, under reflux).
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{CH_3COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

questions.enonce_markdown: State one source and one large scale use of ethanol. Source: ......... Use: ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Source:** fermentation of sugars (for example glucose from sugar cane, or starch from cassava or maize) by yeast: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + 2\mathrm{CO_2}$ (it can also be made by hydration of ethene).

**Large scale use:** as a **fuel** (for example mixed with petrol), or as a solvent, or in the manufacture of alcoholic drinks.
